hosted Core run 36521298082 at 6fc0428b49f28379cb4da17830d92256b55c2eb2 (conclusion success) ran the step 'Run owned CX01 recovery drill evidence' and then 'Require executed CX01 recovery evidence', which asserts skips == Counter() and passed == 20

restatedBlockers.why: PR #126 landed as 9de490fd, so the stated precondition is satisfied and waiting for it would wait forever. Measured at 6fc0428b with a PostgreSQL DSN supplied: 1 passed, 19 skipped, and every skip reason is a container input -- 17 on CX01_CONTAINER and 2 on INV_TEST_ARCHIVER_IMAGE. The count did not move; only the reason did, from a missing DSN to missing container identity.
restatedBlockers.whyTheRestatementWasAlsoWrong: It kept the subject as an external precondition. Hosted Core run 36521298082 at 6fc0428b had already run the drill with 0 skips and 20 passed, so nothing was being waited for. The skips were local to this workstation.

localUnmeasured.condition: 19 of 20 cases need a CX01 container on this host -- 17 for CX01_CONTAINER and 2 for the archiver image, which is that container's image. This workstation has no CX01 container and local docker is off by memory constraint.
localUnmeasured.measuredIn: hosted Core run 36886647197 at 25f43a25 (step 'Require executed CX01 recovery evidence'): 0 skips, 20 passed. Re-measured at this registry's tree; the first measurement was run 36521298082 at 6fc0428b and a claim about a tree has to be shown at that tree.
localUnmeasured.note: Filed as a blocker in registry 1.2.0 and in the restatedBlockers note. That was wrong twice over: first it waited for merged PR #126, then it waited for inputs hosted CI already supplies. A gap in my own measurement is not a gap in the work.

cards.ciVerifiedNote: Re-derived at 25f43a25 and now true. The reason this was false -- no workflow runs tools/collect_s12_acceptance_evidence.py -- stopped being true when .github/workflows/s12-acceptance-evidence.yml landed with #283: CI derives the bundle, holds it to its shape and to the head it was derived at, and uploads it. The restore drill stays ci-verified by core.yml's owned CX01 steps, now at this tree. What is still NOT ci-verified is anything beyond this card: no workflow aggregates the AC-11 axes, and operational acceptance needs a real restore on real hardware.

steps: Derive the AC-12 acceptance items: success

ciVerifiedRun.why: The dispatch at #283's final head, which is an ancestor of this registry's verifiedAgainst.tree. The gate step is what makes it evidence rather than a green tick: check_s12_acceptance_shape.py re-derives the verdict and the seventeen item sources from the collector and refuses a bundle whose codeSha is not the head the run checked out, so a fabricated PASS cannot pass it.
